## A lake of volcanic origin

Lake Coatepeque lies in western El Salvador, in the Santa Ana region. Green slopes surround its blue waters, making it rewarding to visit both the shore and viewpoints above the lake.

Coatepeque is a natural addition to a visit to [Los Volcanes](/el-salvador/place/los-volcanes-national-park/): after forest trails and volcano views, you can stop by the water and enjoy a change of pace.

## Things to do at the lake

Boat trips and water activities, including kayaking, are available on Lake Coatepeque. Along the shore are places to have lunch overlooking the lake. Resident and migratory birds can be found in the surrounding natural area.

The water changes color from time to time, so its famous turquoise hue is not constant. During these changes, local authorities may advise against activities in the water; check which activities are possible before visiting.

## An optional stop

On the [Best of El Salvador](/el-salvador/tour/el-salvador-san-salvador-suchitoto-gulf-of-fonseca/) itinerary, lunch on the shores of Coatepeque is offered as an option on day three. The lake is therefore an optional addition rather than a required stop. You can discuss including it when planning the day between archaeological sites, Santa Ana and Ataco.

The lake stretches through a scenic valley between mountain ranges. Its calm waters, reflecting the surrounding peaks and forests, are particularly striking. The landscape shifts with the weather: sunshine brings out the deep colors of the water, while mist and clouds give the lake an almost mysterious atmosphere.

The road to Escondido passes through one of the most beautiful parts of Tierra del Fuego, crossing mountain passes, ancient forests and broad valleys. Along the way, panoramic views open up across the southern Andes. The lake itself is a wonderful place to stop, take a walk and enjoy photography.

Escondido particularly appeals to travelers who appreciate both well-known attractions and the chance to experience Patagonia's wilderness: quiet, expansive and remarkably beautiful.

Furnas Lake is associated with the hydroelectric power station of the same name and routes through the Capitólio region. From the water, visitors discover canyons and rocky shorelines.

A boat trip offers views of waterfalls and a chance to relax by the water. On motorcycle tours, this day does not involve a long road transfer.
